name: Melle Juric
life: Melle became a speech therapist after learning that her father could name a place if his feet remembered the approach. She buys comfortable shoes before buying a new set of picture cards. On Saturday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Melle checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: My father remembers the coffee seller's face but loses names halfway through a sentence. We walked the old route with no questions until he named her on his own.
appearance: Melle has a round face with a pronounced chin. Look for a blunt cut just below the ears. Out of work clothes, the familiar outfit is a long navy raincoat with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. In conversation Melle turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To give her father a walk on which he can find the name himself.
family: Dominic Alvarez is Melle’s parent’s cousin. Melle leaves the first voice message. Dominic calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The dead man's tab*, Dominic says, “I'm his old victim's sister. I offered to cover only the meals that went to people still alive.”
connections: Elsa Venn. They walk the likely street with somebody who remembers a face more easily than a name.

reactions.situation: A family member disputes the penciled street
reactions.response: Melle marks the disputed piece of street in pencil and keeps the alternative name beside it.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Melle finds a second person to witness its return so an honest mistake won't cost a worker their pay.
